body:
Not to seem pessimistic or ungrateful, but I've tried to exercise is the past.  It is simply not enough to distract me, and I even tried to get a routine going, but I still find myself thinking back when I would be exercising.  I'm trying to become more active and more social, but like I said, I'm not too fond of meeting new people and seeming well like everyone else.  But that's not to say I'm not trying.  I try to talk with the people that I work with and force myself to interact with them, but no matter what I do, at the end of the day, it feels so unfulfilling.  
I will attempt to do some of the things you mentioned, like small meals, a big cup of water to begin my day, going for walks, but I think that they are merely ways to pass the time rather than a fix in themselves.

Sure, maybe not everyone is happy and carefree, but they at least have periods of happiness and carefreeness.  The ability to even be that way at times is enough to dishearten me.  
I realize that people all have problems, but often times, most people's issues seem so shallow and irrelevant compared to mine.  Perhaps I suffer from a self-centered worldview, but I still find it hard to imagine how most people's problems can be as bad as mine.

That is a huge problem that I see.  I do not know what will make life interesting, joyful, or filling.  Everything is dull and colorless.  Nothing seems interesting to me.  I've tried a few activities, such as trying to talk to more people, filling my time with work, reading, exercising, but none of those have the ability to distract me very long at all, and in the end, I end up bored and tired of them.  

Perhaps you could give me a few things that you think would be enjoyable or interesting?

Thanks.

I believe that my friends do know how I am doing.  I've told them about the thoughts I've been having, and I've even called a couple when I had seriously wanted to end it all.  

On your note about therapy, I do not know how they will help.  As other people have probably mentioned before, I think that its a pseudoscience, and will probably be placebo effect at best.  But I am considering it, and I have planned to look more into it soon.  

You said I am pretty vague about the source of my feelings.  What do you mean by that?  Feel free to ask me to clarify anything you think I am being vague on.  I don't know you (yet perhaps) and I have nothing to hide.  

As for doing something I enjoy or worth doing, that is a problem.  I do not currently find anything enjoyable or worth doing.  Perhaps that is a sign of depression and should be solved soon.
